# Zoom Events sessions record Zoom's window again, not the whole screen {camcorder}
A Zoom Events session names its window after the session -- "Joey Yap's
BaZi Health Mastery" -- and the test that chooses between recording Zoom's
window and recording the screen only accepted "Zoom Meeting" or "Zoom
Webinar". So the capture found that window, settled on it, and four seconds
later decided there was no window to record and filmed the whole desktop
instead: a two-hour class, with everything else on the screen in it. The
alert that explained it blamed screen sharing which never happened.
Ordinary meetings and plain webinars were never affected. A window Zoom has
NAMED still wins; one it has not is now recorded rather than abandoned, and
a capture that does go to the screen can find its way back.

# The live transcript stopped guessing, and got quicker {mic}
Two faults, both invisible. The resident speech model was dying before the
first word of every meeting -- it was being handed six-tenths of a second
of silence to warm up on, which is the one thing it cannot take -- so the
whole hour was transcribed a sentence at a time, at twice the work per
sentence, and the words arrived a beat behind the voice. And where the
model had measured nothing about how sure it was, the app filled the gap
with CERTAINTY: a line could decide what language your whole meeting was
in on a number that did not exist. It says "unknown" now, nothing decides
anything from it, and the first thing said in a meeting is kept while the
model gets ready rather than dropped to make room.

---

Everything else in this release:

- **"Transcribe again" no longer makes every line early.** Reading a
  finished recording put each line's start exactly where the line before
  it ended, so a transcript followed along beside the video jumped to the
  next line the moment the last one finished instead of waiting for
  anybody to speak -- and a one-word answer could be stretched across
  nine seconds of silence. The cause was the silence filter: it reads the
  speech with the quiet cut out, then puts the times back by spreading
  them over the gaps it removed. The recording is read as it is now, and
  the invented lines that filter existed to prevent -- the sentence
  repeated over the last nine seconds of nothing, the stray "OK" -- are
  found in the audio instead and dropped, with a line in the log saying
  which. On the recording this was reported from: twenty-three lines
  where the words actually are, and the two nobody said, gone.

- **A meeting is no longer decided by one sentence.** What language the app
  thinks a meeting is in used to be settled by the first confident reading
  and then imposed on every short answer -- so one misheard "hello" could
  put an English meeting into Malay and keep it there, and somebody who
  switched language for a single sentence could not be transcribed in it.
  It is now weighed from whole sentences over the last few minutes, it
  fades when nobody says anything for a while, and it is only ever used to
  decide what SHORT answers are read as. Every line is written in the
  language it was actually heard in, and a line that was read under that
  guess says so, so the second pass can look at it again.

- The speech model no longer falls over on a room. Silence, a hum from the
  mains, a fan, a tone, somebody typing -- anything with no speech in it --
  made the resident model exit, and each time it did, the rest of the
  meeting was transcribed the slow way. It returns an empty line and keeps
  going now. (The fault was in whisper.cpp itself, which we build; the fix
  is a patch we carry and a note for whoever rebuilds it.)

- **The app asks which language your meetings are in, once, instead of
  choosing for you.** Both of the answers it could have picked are
  measured and both are bad. Detecting the language reads plain
  Singapore English as MALAY at 75% on the model this app ships, and
  writes it down in Malay. Assuming English does something worse: a
  meeting held in Mandarin, Malay or Tamil comes back as fluent,
  confident English, and nothing in the transcript says it was
  translated. So when you switch live transcription on, it asks --
  English, Chinese, Malay, Tamil, or Automatic, which says it is
  experimental -- with your Mac's own language already highlighted. You
  can change it any time, and the language it is listening for is shown
  while it runs.
- **The "English + Chinese" style mixed-language choices are switched off
  for now.** They read each sentence twice, once in each language, and kept
  whichever scored better -- and on six seconds of plain English from a real
  meeting, a wholly invented Chinese reading scored 0.83 against the correct
  English at 0.72. It would have chosen the invention. If you had one of
  those chosen, your choice is remembered and your meetings are transcribed
  in English until the picking is fixed; the Language row says so.
- The transcript no longer promises that nothing leaves your Mac, because
  the optional AI features send the recording to whichever provider you
  pick. Live transcription itself still runs entirely on this Mac.
- The language menu no longer claims that a sentence with two languages
  inside it comes out right. It cannot: the speech model reads a stretch of
  audio as ONE language, so a mixed sentence comes back as one of them.
  People taking turns in different languages is the case that works, and
  that is what it says now.
- A line the model scored badly says "Unclear audio" instead of "low
  confidence". The number behind it describes how the decoding went, not
  whether the words are right, and it was never a percentage of anything.
- Whose voice a line was is no longer stated more firmly than it can be.
  Your own microphone is measured, so that still reads "You"; a name read
  from Zoom's window reads "Likely Mark", two people talking at once reads
  "Multiple speakers", and the meeting's own audio says so rather than
  standing in for a person.
- A transcript now records what the language detector actually said, beside
  what the words were read as. When the two disagree -- which is most of
  the Malay-for-English problem -- it is in the file rather than lost.
- Every frame of audio the transcriber loses is now counted. One truncated
  frame costs two, and only one of them was ever reported.
- **Handouts, while the meeting runs.** The recording page now has a
  Handouts card: whether they are being collected, how often it looks,
  how many times it has looked and when, what the last look found, and
  the files by name with a tick against the ones saved. It is switchable
  per webinar there -- on now, and next time -- and turning it on reaches
  a recording that is already running, within a minute, including
  handouts the host attached before you asked. A webinar whose files Zoom
  had already downloaded used to show nothing at all; it now says so and
  names them. The word is "Handouts" everywhere, where the card said
  "Resources", Settings said "handouts" and Zoom says "Documents".
- **The guide is one guide of eight steps, and it shows you a
  recording.** It used to stop at four and leave the rest until the first
  time you happened to be looking at a run, so most people never saw
  them. The last four are walked on an EXAMPLE recording the guide puts
  up -- a meeting in the list marked Recording, with a live transcript
  filling in and the switches on the page -- and every control in it is
  inert. Anybody who updates and has not seen the guide is offered it,
  and anybody who saw the old four-step one is offered the four about a
  recording. The step's own row is what lights up now; everything else on
  the page fades.
- **Collecting the logs no longer freezes the window.** It ran the whole
  preflight -- a screen-capture probe, launchctl, system_profiler and an
  ffmpeg device scan with no time limit -- on the thread that draws, so
  exporting during a live meeting could stop the app answering for as
  long as the audio system made it wait. Reported as an app that hung and
  then would not open. The device scan now has an end, and the export
  happens on a thread with its own line in the footer.
- **A laugh is no longer a line in the transcript.** whisper writes what
  subtitles are full of -- "[LAUGHTER]", "[Music]", "Thanks for watching"
  -- and the live listener has always taken those out. Reading a
  recording again did not, so the same meeting could have a clean live
  transcript and a re-read full of annotations nobody said. Somebody
  laughing out loud still reads as words, because that is what was said.
- **A transcript in more than one language can be read again if you
  insist.** It is left alone by default, because a whole-file pass reads
  ONE language: measured on a real meeting, forcing it gave cleaner
  English throughout and dropped both of its Chinese lines. That is a
  judgement rather than a fault, so the button now says what it would
  cost and lets you decide.
- **A warning before a scheduled meeting if this Mac is on battery**,
  with the charge, and a stronger one if macOS has given up on the
  battery -- which is the state that cost a colleague an hour-long class
  on a Mac that reported a healthy-looking charge and slept anyway.
- **Setting up phone alerts says where the app comes from.** "Install the
  ntfy app" assumed you knew what ntfy was; it now names the App Store
  and Google Play, what to search for, and which control to look for once
  it is open.
